source: LCME Functions and Structure of a Medical School, 2025-26

standards.title: Mission, Planning, Organization, and Integrity
standards.summary: Written statement of mission and goals, ongoing planning, written bylaws, effective organizational structure, integrity in all activities.

elements.title: Strategic Planning and Continuous Quality Improvement
elements.summary: Ongoing strategic planning and CQI processes with measurable outcomes to improve program quality and monitor accreditation compliance.

elements.title: Conflict of Interest
elements.summary: Effective policies for board members, faculty, and others to avoid conflicts of interest in medical education program operations.

elements.title: Mechanisms for Faculty Participation
elements.summary: Effective mechanisms for direct faculty participation in decision-making related to the medical education program.

elements.title: Affiliation Agreements
elements.summary: Written affiliation agreements with clinical affiliates specifying responsibilities, student/faculty access, academic authority, and learning environment.

elements.title: Bylaws
elements.summary: Bylaws or similar documents describing responsibilities and privileges of administrative officers, faculty, and committees.

elements.title: Eligibility Requirements
elements.summary: Medical education program meets all LCME eligibility requirements including degree-granting authority and regional accreditation.

standards.title: Leadership and Administration
standards.summary: Sufficient faculty in leadership roles and senior administrative staff with skills, time, and support to achieve program goals.

elements.title: Administrative Officer and Faculty Appointments
elements.summary: Senior administrative staff and faculty appointed by or on authority of the governing board.

elements.title: Dean's Qualifications
elements.summary: Dean qualified by education, training, and experience for effective leadership in medical education, scholarly activity, and patient care.

elements.title: Access and Authority of the Dean
elements.summary: Dean has sufficient access to institutional officials and clear definition of authority and responsibility for the program.

elements.title: Sufficiency of Administrative Staff
elements.summary: Sufficient associate/assistant deans, unit leaders, and senior administrative staff able to commit necessary time.

elements.title: Responsibility of and to the Dean
elements.summary: Dean administratively responsible for conduct and quality of the program; principal academic officers at regional campuses report to dean.

elements.title: Functional Integration of the Faculty
elements.summary: Faculty at all campuses functionally integrated through appropriate administrative mechanisms.

standards.title: Academic and Learning Environments
standards.summary: Professional, respectful, intellectually stimulating environments that recognize diversity benefits and promote required competencies.

elements.title: Resident Participation in Medical Student Education
elements.summary: Each student participates in required clinical experiences with resident physicians in accredited GME programs.

elements.title: Community of Scholars/Research Opportunities
elements.summary: Environment fosters intellectual challenge and spirit of inquiry with sufficient opportunities for student research participation.

elements.title: Diversity/Pipeline Programs and Partnerships
elements.summary: Effective policies and systematic recruitment/retention activities to achieve mission-appropriate diversity outcomes.

elements.title: Anti-Discrimination Policy
elements.summary: Policy ensuring no discrimination on basis of age, disability, gender identity, national origin, race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, or federal protected basis.

elements.title: Learning Environment/Professionalism
elements.summary: Learning environment conducive to professional behaviors; periodic evaluation to enhance positive and mitigate negative influences.

elements.title: Student Mistreatment
elements.summary: Written mistreatment policies, prompt response mechanisms, educational activities for prevention, and reporting without fear of retaliation.

standards.title: Faculty Preparation, Productivity, Participation, and Policies
standards.summary: Faculty qualified through education, training, experience, and continuing professional development to support institutional goals.

elements.title: Sufficiency of Faculty
elements.summary: Sufficient faculty cohort with qualifications and time to deliver curriculum and meet institutional missions.

elements.title: Scholarly Productivity
elements.summary: Faculty demonstrate commitment to continuing scholarly productivity characteristic of higher learning.

elements.title: Faculty Appointment Policies
elements.summary: Clear policies for appointment, renewal, promotion, tenure, remediation, and dismissal with written information for each faculty member.

elements.title: Feedback to Faculty
elements.summary: Regularly scheduled and timely feedback on academic performance and progress toward promotion/tenure.

elements.title: Faculty Professional Development
elements.summary: Opportunities for professional development in discipline content, curricular design, program evaluation, assessment, instructional methodology, and research.

elements.title: Responsibility for Medical School Policies
elements.summary: Dean and faculty committee determine governance and policymaking processes within their purview.

standards.title: Educational Resources and Infrastructure
standards.summary: Sufficient personnel, financial resources, facilities, equipment, and clinical/informational/technological resources across all locations.

elements.title: Adequacy of Financial Resources
elements.summary: Financial resources from diverse sources adequate to sustain sound medical education and accomplish institutional goals.

elements.title: Dean's Authority/Resources
elements.summary: Dean has sufficient resources and budgetary authority for management and evaluation of the medical curriculum.

elements.title: Pressures for Self-Financing
elements.summary: School admits only as many applicants as resources accommodate; financial influences do not compromise educational mission.

elements.title: Sufficiency of Buildings and Equipment
elements.summary: Buildings and equipment sufficient for educational, clinical, and research missions.

elements.title: Resources for Clinical Instruction
elements.summary: Appropriate resources for clinical instruction in ambulatory and inpatient settings with adequate patient numbers and types.

elements.title: Clinical Instructional Facilities/Information Resources
elements.summary: Affiliated clinical facilities have sufficient information resources and instructional facilities.

elements.title: Security, Student Safety, and Disaster Preparedness
elements.summary: Adequate security systems, published safety policies, and emergency/disaster preparedness at all locations.

elements.title: Library Resources/Staff
elements.summary: Ready access to well-maintained library resources with professional staff familiar with regional/national information systems.

elements.title: Information Technology Resources/Staff
elements.summary: Access to well-maintained IT resources with sufficient staff expertise responsive to institutional needs.

elements.title: Resources Used by Transfer/Visiting Students
elements.summary: Resources for visiting/transfer students do not significantly diminish resources for enrolled students.

elements.title: Study/Lounge/Storage Space/Call Rooms
elements.summary: Adequate study space, lounge areas, secure storage, and call rooms at each campus and clinical site.

elements.title: Required Notifications to the LCME
elements.summary: School notifies LCME of substantial changes in enrollment, resources, curriculum modifications, or affiliation status changes.

standards.title: Competencies, Curricular Objectives, and Curricular Design
standards.summary: Faculty define competencies through program objectives and design curriculum components enabling students to achieve them.

elements.title: Program and Learning Objectives
elements.summary: Faculty define outcome-based program objectives allowing assessment of student progress; objectives known to all students and faculty.

elements.title: Required Clinical Experiences
elements.summary: Faculty define required patient types, clinical conditions, student skills, appropriate settings, and expected levels of responsibility.

elements.title: Self-Directed and Life-Long Learning
elements.summary: Curriculum includes self-directed learning experiences and unscheduled time for developing lifelong learning skills.

elements.title: Inpatient/Outpatient Experiences
elements.summary: Curriculum includes clinical experiences in both outpatient and inpatient settings.

elements.title: Elective Opportunities
elements.summary: Elective opportunities supplement required experiences, permitting exposure to specialties and individual academic interests.

elements.title: Service-Learning/Community Service
elements.summary: Sufficient opportunities for, encouragement of, and support for student participation in service-learning and community service.

elements.title: Academic Environments
elements.summary: Opportunities for interaction with other health professions students and physicians in GME and CME programs.

elements.title: Education Program Duration
elements.summary: Medical education program includes at least 130 weeks of instruction.

standards.title: Curricular Content
standards.summary: Curriculum provides content of sufficient breadth and depth to prepare students for entry into any residency program.

elements.title: Biomedical, Behavioral, Social Sciences
elements.summary: Content from biomedical, behavioral, and socioeconomic sciences supporting mastery of contemporary medical science knowledge and concepts.

elements.title: Organ Systems/Life Cycle/Prevention/Symptoms/Signs/Differential Diagnosis, Treatment Planning
elements.summary: Content and clinical experiences related to each organ system, life cycle phase, and continuity/preventive/acute/chronic/rehabilitative/end-of-life care.

elements.title: Scientific Method/Clinical/Translational Research
elements.summary: Instruction in scientific method and basic scientific/ethical principles of clinical and translational research.

elements.title: Critical Judgment/Problem-Solving Skills
elements.summary: Fundamental principles of medicine, skills of critical judgment based on evidence and experience, and effective problem-solving.

elements.title: Societal Problems
elements.summary: Instruction in diagnosis, prevention, appropriate reporting, and treatment of medical consequences of common societal problems.

elements.title: Cultural Competence and Health Care Disparities
elements.summary: Opportunities to recognize and address biases; culturally competent care; health care disparities; multidimensional diverse society.

elements.title: Medical Ethics
elements.summary: Instruction in medical ethics and human values prior to and during patient care activities; ethical behavior in caring for patients.

elements.title: Communication Skills
elements.summary: Specific instruction in communication skills with patients, families, colleagues, and other health professionals.

elements.title: Interprofessional Collaborative Skills
elements.summary: Core curriculum prepares students to function collaboratively on interprofessional health care teams.

standards.title: Curricular Management, Evaluation, and Enhancement
standards.summary: Faculty engage in curricular revision and program evaluation to maintain/enhance quality and ensure students achieve all objectives.

elements.title: Curricular Management
elements.summary: Faculty committee oversees the medical education program with responsibility for overall design, management, integration, evaluation, and enhancement.

elements.title: Use of Medical Educational Program Objectives
elements.summary: Program objectives guide curriculum content selection; course/clerkship learning objectives linked to program objectives.

elements.title: Curricular Design, Review, Revision/Content Monitoring
elements.summary: Faculty committee responsible for detailed development, design, implementation, and ongoing monitoring of all curriculum components.

elements.title: Evaluation of Educational Program Outcomes
elements.summary: Variety of outcome data including national norms used to demonstrate student achievement and enhance program quality.

elements.title: Medical Student Feedback
elements.summary: Formal processes to collect and consider student evaluations of courses, clerkships, teachers, and other relevant information.

elements.title: Monitoring of Completion of Required Clinical Experiences
elements.summary: Central oversight system monitors and ensures completion of required clinical experiences and remedies gaps.

elements.title: Comparability of Education/Assessment
elements.summary: Comparable educational experiences and equivalent assessment methods across all locations within courses and clerkships.

elements.title: Monitoring Student Time
elements.summary: Effective policies regarding amount of time students spend in required activities including clinical and educational hours during clerkships.

standards.title: Teaching, Supervision, Assessment, and Student and Patient Safety
standards.summary: Comprehensive, fair, uniform assessment system; all teachers/supervisors/assessors adequately prepared for their responsibilities.

elements.title: Preparation of Resident and Non-Faculty Instructors
elements.summary: Residents and non-faculty instructors familiar with learning objectives and prepared for teaching/assessment roles with skill enhancement resources.

elements.title: Faculty Appointments
elements.summary: Supervision of student learning experiences provided by faculty members throughout required clerkships.

elements.title: Clinical Supervision of Medical Students
elements.summary: Appropriate supervision at all times for patient safety and student safety; delegated responsibility appropriate to training level.

elements.title: Assessment System
elements.summary: Centralized system employing variety of measures including direct observation for assessing student achievement of program objectives.

elements.title: Narrative Assessment
elements.summary: Narrative description of student performance including non-cognitive achievement in each required course/clerkship where interaction permits.

elements.title: Setting Standards of Achievement
elements.summary: Faculty with appropriate knowledge and expertise set standards of achievement in each required learning experience.

elements.title: Formative Assessment and Feedback
elements.summary: Each student assessed and provided formal formative feedback early enough for remediation, at least at midpoint.

elements.title: Fair and Timely Summative Assessment
elements.summary: Fair and timely summative assessment system; final grades available within six weeks of course/clerkship end.

elements.title: Student Advancement and Appeal Process
elements.summary: Single set of core standards for advancement/graduation across all locations; fair and formal process for actions affecting student status.

standards.title: Medical Student Selection, Assignment, and Progress
standards.summary: Published admission requirements with effective policies for student selection, enrollment, and assignment.

elements.title: Premedical Education/Required Coursework
elements.summary: Requirements encourage broad undergraduate education; specific premedical requirements confined to essential preparation.

elements.title: Final Authority of Admission Committee
elements.summary: Formally constituted admission committee with faculty majority has final responsibility for accepting students; no political/financial influence.

elements.title: Policies Regarding Student Selection/Progress and Their Dissemination
elements.summary: Faculty establish criteria and implement effective policies for application, selection, admission, assessment, promotion, graduation, and discipline.

elements.title: Characteristics of Accepted Applicants
elements.summary: Applicants possess intelligence, integrity, and personal/emotional characteristics necessary for physician competence.

elements.title: Technical Standards
elements.summary: Published technical standards for admission, retention, and graduation in accordance with legal requirements.

elements.title: Content of Informational Materials
elements.summary: Accurate representation of mission, objectives, degree requirements, academic calendar, and required courses/clerkships.

elements.title: Transfer Students
elements.summary: Transfer students demonstrate comparable achievements; final-year transfer only in rare and extraordinary circumstances.

elements.title: Visiting Students
elements.summary: Credential verification, qualification comparison, roster maintenance, assignment approval, performance assessment, and health protocols for visitors.

elements.title: Student Assignment
elements.summary: School assumes ultimate responsibility for student selection and assignment to each location/track with process for alternative requests.

standards.title: Medical Student Academic Support, Career Advising, and Educational Records
standards.summary: Effective academic support and career advising to assist students in achieving career goals and program objectives.

elements.title: Academic Advising
elements.summary: Effective academic advising integrating faculty, course/clerkship directors, student affairs, counseling, and tutorial services.

elements.title: Career Advising
elements.summary: Effective career advising integrating faculty, clerkship directors, and student affairs for electives, career options, and residency applications.

elements.title: Oversight of Extramural Electives
elements.summary: Centralized system to review proposed extramural electives, ensure performance assessment return, and evaluate risks.

elements.title: Provision of MSPE
elements.summary: Medical Student Performance Evaluation provided only on or after October 1 of the student's final year.

elements.title: Confidentiality of Student Educational Records
elements.summary: Educational records confidential and available only to those with need to know unless released by student or governed by law.

elements.title: Student Access to Educational Records
elements.summary: Students can review and challenge their educational records including MSPE if considered inaccurate, misleading, or inappropriate.

standards.title: Medical Student Health Services, Personal Counseling, and Financial Aid Services
standards.summary: Effective student services to assist in achieving program goals; all students have same rights and receive comparable services.

elements.title: Financial Aid/Debt Management Counseling/Student Educational Debt
elements.summary: Effective financial aid and debt management counseling with mechanisms to minimize impact of direct educational expenses.

elements.title: Tuition Refund Policy
elements.summary: Clear policies for refund of tuition, fees, and other allowable payments following withdrawal.

elements.title: Personal Counseling/Well-Being Programs
elements.summary: Effective personal counseling system with well-being programs facilitating adjustment to medical education demands.

elements.title: Student Access to Health Care Services
elements.summary: Timely access to diagnostic, preventive, and therapeutic health services in reasonable proximity with excusal policies.

elements.title: Non-Involvement of Providers of Student Health Services in Student Assessment/Location of Student Health Records
elements.summary: Health providers not involved in academic assessment/promotion of students they serve; health records maintained per legal requirements.

elements.title: Student Health and Disability Insurance
elements.summary: Health and disability insurance available to each student; health insurance also available for dependents.

elements.title: Immunization Requirements and Monitoring
elements.summary: Accepted guidelines for immunization requirements with student compliance monitoring.

elements.title: Student Exposure Policies/Procedures
elements.summary: Policies for infectious/environmental hazard exposure including education, care/treatment procedures, financial responsibility, and impact on learning.
